idiom_name: functional interface (java.util.function) with lambdas; CompletionStage for completion
implementation_notes: The classic structure - a hand-written Callback interface implemented by an anonymous inner class - is replaced by the java.util.function types with lambdas (Java 8+): Consumer<T>, Runnable, BiFunction and friends are the callback types and the compiler converts a lambda or method reference to them. For asynchronous completion the standard form is to compose a result rather than pass a callback into the callee: CompletableFuture.thenAccept/whenComplete register callbacks on the completed stage, with the *Async variants running on ForkJoinPool.commonPool() unless an executor is supplied, and virtual threads (Java 21) remove the need to invert control merely to avoid a parked platform thread. Keep a named listener interface where the callback must be unregistered by identity, has several methods, or is a published contract (PropertyChangeListener).
pitfalls: Listener registration holds a strong reference, so a listener that is never removed keeps the subscriber alive (the classic Swing/PropertyChangeListener leak); unregister on teardown or use weak listeners.
Lambdas capture only effectively-final locals, and capturing this implicitly (inside an inner class or a getter) keeps the enclosing instance reachable for the registration's lifetime.
An exception thrown in a callback does not reach the initiator: on a CompletionStage it surfaces later as a CompletionException, in an executor it is parked in the Future and only appears on get().
Callbacks executed while a lock is held, or blocking on ForkJoinPool.commonPool(), can deadlock or starve unrelated work; blocking completions need a dedicated executor.
